paper.title: Thompson Sampling for Budgeted Multi-armed Bandits

unmapped: single resource: each pull incurs a random cost in [0,1], independent of the reward; game stops when budget B is exhausted (no time horizon); regret measured as a function of the budget B
optimal arm defined by maximum expected-reward-to-expected-cost ratio
settings.definition_quote: At round $t$, a player pulls an arm $i\in[K]$, receives a random reward $r_i(t)$, and pays a random cost $c_i(t)$ until he runs out of his budget $B$, which is a positive integer.  Both the reward $r_i(t)$ and the cost $c_i(t)$ are supported on $[0,1]$. ... (i) the rewards of an arm are independent of its costs; (ii) ... (iii) the rewards and costs of the same arm at different rounds are independent and identically distributed.

symbols.B_budget: budget B (plays the role of the horizon)
symbols.Phi_i: O(1/eps_i^4) if mu_1^c+eps_i>=1, else O(1/(eps_i^6 (1-mu_1^c-eps_i))), eps_i=(1-gamma)mu_1^c Delta_i/(mu_i^r/mu_i^c+1); independent of B

conditions: reward independent of cost for each arm
mu_i^r > 0 and mu_i^c > 0 for all arms
arm 1 is the unique arm maximizing mu^r/mu^c

source.label: thm:bound_TS_asymp
source.quote: $\forall \gamma \in (0,1)$, for both Bernoulli bandits and general bandits, the regret of the BTS algorithm can be upper bounded as below. \textrm{Regret} \leq \sum_{i=2}^{K}\Big\{\frac{2\ln B}{\gamma^2\mu_i^c\Delta_i}\bigg(\frac{\mu_1^r}{\mu_1^c}+1\bigg)^2 + \Phi_i(\gamma)\Big\}+O\bigg(\frac{K}{\gamma^2}\bigg)

results.notes: Leading ln B term is explicit; remaining terms in O(·) with constants depending on instance means. Holds for both Bernoulli and general [0,1] bandits (Bernoulli case not recorded separately). Regret is R* minus expected reward, R* being the optimal policy's expected reward. Remark 2 with gamma=1/sqrt(2) gives leading constant 4(mu_1^r/mu_1^c+1)^2 sum 1/(mu_i^c Delta_i). The appendix uses B > e. Theorem number assumed 'Theorem 1' — counter shared with lemmas, so the printed number may differ (Lemmas 1,2 precede, so possibly Theorem 3).
